editorial.headline: Used Construction and Sanitary Goods: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers retail trade in used building and sanitary materials, with full foreign ownership nationally but a permanent PMA block in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 47745 is the retail activity for used construction and sanitary goods. Its scope includes second-hand building materials and used sanitary items such as washbasins, toilets and water tanks; it also expressly notes direct sales. The commercial centre of gravity is clear: this is a trade classification for selling previously used fixtures and materials to end buyers, rather than for their manufacture or installation.

The activity is open to businesses at every stated scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership level of 100%. In practical terms, the national classification permits full foreign ownership for this activity, subject to the scope described in the record.

Bali is the decisive qualification. A foreign investor cannot register this activity under PMA in Bali today. At the Besar scale, OSS risk is classified as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every scope, placing the activity within Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium on PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. The block is therefore not a question of the national ownership ceiling: it arises from Bali’s risk-based provincial restriction.

For founders, that distinction matters. The national framework says the activity is open and can be wholly foreign-owned; Bali’s framework says PMA registration is blocked. A plan centred on retailing used sanitary fixtures or construction materials in Bali must be read through that local constraint, not merely through the national foreign-ownership position.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally this activity permits full foreign ownership, but Bali’s risk-based moratorium blocks PMA registration.
